classification.difficultyReason: Transfer the tangent–chord angle to the supplied opposite vertex, then use supplementary opposite angles in the cyclic quadrilateral.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Four vertices on a circle; three solid chords form the left triangle. Two dashed auxiliary chords join the top and contact vertices through the lower-right vertex. A sloping tangent touches the bottom-left vertex. The 70° sector runs from the chord towards the top vertex to the upper-left tangent ray; x is the interior angle at the upper-left vertex. Decorative source pink and teal are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The tangent–chord angle is 70°. The angle at the lower-right vertex subtending the top-to-contact chord is therefore 70°. Its opposite cyclic-quadrilateral angle is x=110°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only x and the given 70° appear in the question diagram; the supplied 110° answer is excluded.

answer.worked:
The angle at the lower-right vertex is $70^\circ$ by the alternate segment theorem. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}x+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\x&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$
